analysis.title: Euro rates have good reason to be nervous
key_insights: ING sees substantial near-term upside risk to euro rates but a more constructive year-end outlook. Easing inflation fears should bring euro rates down by mid-2027, but the path will be bumpy.
Baseline: inflation pressures ease and the ECB terminal rate anchors near 2.5% by end-2027. Heavy global bond supply should keep long-dated rates relatively elevated.
Second-round inflation fears could push the 10-year euro swap rate above 4%. Faster disinflation could take it towards 2%.
For 2027 the focus shifts from oil to inflation data. Even with oil below $80/bbl in the baseline, swap rates would not find much immediate relief.

One bad inflation reading could spook markets and risk a repeat of 2022-23, while a series of benign readings is needed to convince markets of a dovish tilt. ING therefore sees limited downside to rates in 1H27.

Markets price 1Y1Y forward inflation at 2.2%, which implies strong confidence in the ECB and is consistent with three further ECB hikes being priced. Policy effectiveness during supply shocks may be limited.

AI investment is unlikely to respond to a few 25bp hikes while earnings growth is in double digits. Perceived weaker policy transmission plus upside inflation surprises could push 2-year euro swap rates another 100bp higher.

A dovish shift in the ECB reaction function is an unpriced risk. 5y5y inflation swaps at 2.1% show little risk priced to the 2% target. France could force the ECB to keep financial conditions supportive, possibly halting QT. ING says to brace for significantly steeper curves if this happens.

Longer-dated real rates are being pushed higher globally, led by the US. QT at all major central banks and rising government debt add bond supply, so 10-year euro swap rates should stay sticky at elevated levels even as 2-year rates fall.

Rising private-sector borrowing, including AI-driven investment, is a wildcard that could lift global rates further. It is not the baseline because higher rates should weigh on investment appetite, and outside technology the investment boom is not convincing.
ING says markets in 2026 have overshot in repricing the terminal ECB rate. A rate above 3% is hard to reconcile with the prior 1.75-2.25% range.
The 10-year swap rate is close to fair value against nominal growth expectations of 3.3%, which limits downside for 10-year rates.

risk_factors: Second-round inflation effects triggering a repeat of 2022-23 rate moves.
Rising inflation combined with an ECB unable to stem it, because policy may be less effective during supply shocks.
An ECB forced to tolerate higher inflation, with France's spreads as the trigger, producing significantly steeper curves.
Perceived weaker monetary policy transmission pushing 2-year euro swap rates another 100bp higher.
Higher global bond supply from QT, government debt and possible private-sector borrowing, including AI investment, keeping long-dated rates elevated.
geopolitical: Energy prices are still far from settled and the global geopolitical landscape remains unstable.
France could face wider bond spreads if rates rise, which could force the ECB to keep financial conditions supportive.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation pressures ease and the ECB terminal rate anchors near 2.5% by end-2027. Faster disinflation could take the 10-year swap rate towards 2%.
tension_points.bear_case: Second-round inflation effects could push the 10-year swap rate above 4%, and a weaker policy transmission could lift 2-year swap rates another 100bp.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A single bad inflation reading showing second-round effects could spook markets and risk a repeat of 2022-23.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price 1Y1Y inflation at 2.2% and 5y5y at 2.1%, showing confidence the ECB returns inflation to target.
tension_points.bear_case: France-driven spread widening could force the ECB to tolerate higher inflation and halt QT, which is not priced in 5y5y swaps and would steepen curves significantly.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Higher rates widening French bond spreads and forcing the ECB to keep financial conditions supportive.
